title: Rabbit Season
summary: Horned rabbits ate a farmer's carrots. One of them is enormous.

title: Slime in the Well
summary: Blue slimes have moved into Millbrook's well. Gently remove them, or don't be gentle.

title: The Goblin Chief of Hollowpine
summary: The F→E promotion trial: defeat the goblin chief leading organized raids from Hollowpine.

title: The Silver Wolf of Mistvale
summary: Livestock vanish under the full moon. Witnesses describe a wolf of silver light.

title: Status Granted
summary: You wake in a Whisperwood clearing under two moons. A slime watches you. Survive the night, then follow Lyra to town.

title: The Wooden Card
summary: Register at the Guild. The appraisal crystal flickers strangely, and Mina covers for it.

title: A Bowl of Stew
summary: Marta feeds you on credit. Brother Caspian arrives with the orphans and offers you a blanket and a place to sleep.

title: Mina's Lost Earring
summary: A giant crow stole Mina's earring. Its nest is full of shiny things.

title: The Crying Mandrake
summary: Fennick needs mandrake roots. One of them is a baby, and its mother is very large.

title: A Thousand Swings
summary: Swing at the training post at dawn for seven days, then beat Hollis. He uses a broom.

title: The Tavern Brawl
summary: Brutus mocks your wooden card one time too many. One punch later, the whole tavern learns what you really are.

title: Goblins in the Granary
summary: Goblins raid Hesk's granary every night. One of them is a starving child sent to scout.

title: Night of the Smiling Scarecrow
summary: The scarecrow in Odo's east field is in a different field every morning. Watch it at night. Don't look away.

title: The Mural of Nine Thrones
summary: Eolande wants a sketch of the mural in the Whisperwood ruins. It shows nine thrones. One has been scratched out.

title: The Crimson Wolves
summary: Dax challenges you to a race: whoever clears the wolf den first takes the bounty. Pim has already cheated.

title: Hold the Line: {settlement}
summary: Template for Whisperwood siege attacks. Grukk's warband will hit {settlement} at dusk tomorrow. Set barricades and traps, then hold for three waves (Data/World/siege_waves.json).

title: Whisperwood Hunting Contract
summary: Template for post-liberation hunting work: the guild posts culls for whatever is breeding near the roads now that the goblin raids have stopped.

title: Payday at the Griffon
summary: Payday means drinking, and drinking means fists. Marta needs someone sober by the door.

title: The Stable Boy's Broom
summary: Teo has been sneaking out at night. He asks you to come and say nothing.

title: The Boy on the North Road
summary: Teo has followed a party north to "help". Marta asks you to bring him home, and not to shame him.

title: Every Bed in the Griffon
summary: Marrowgate is gone and the refugees have nowhere to go. Marta has forty beds and sixty people.

title: Edric's Sword
summary: Marta takes her husband's sword off the wall and asks you to carry it to Brannoc.

title: The North Road Ledger
summary: Wendel has found a line in the town accounts that matches no road. He asks you to look, because he cannot.

title: Tomlin Tries Again
summary: Tomlin failed the registration appraisal on one question. He asks you to help him answer it.

title: The Count at the Gate
summary: A surge of undead walks the north road. Holt needs another set of eyes on the gate, and an honest count at dawn.

title: Candles for the Hall
summary: The guild hall's candles are low. Aster asks you to carry a bundle to Wendel, and to stay for tea.

title: The Sound of Rank
summary: The blind fiddler claims he can tell your rank by the sound of your steps. He asks you to prove him wrong.

title: Joren's Last Contract
summary: Joren was gathering moon-moss for his mother's wicks when he died. Aster asks you to finish the contract.

title: Lantern Night in Brindlewick
summary: Every autumn the town lights a lantern for each name in the Hall of Cards. Aster shows you how to make one.

title: The Tune Under the Hymn
summary: Corwin heard the orphans singing at noon and dropped his bow. He knows the tune. He does not know why.

title: Boxing Barn
summary: Sister Pell boxes in the barn behind the shrine on weekends. She says a good cleric is a good guard first.

title: The Inquisitor at the Shrine
summary: An Inquisitor has arrived in Brindlewick. Pell goes white, and asks you not to say she is here.

title: The Quiet Pharmacy
summary: Fennick sends a parcel of medicine somewhere every month. This month he cannot carry it.

title: A Letter in a Familiar Hand
summary: Pell has received a letter in Sister Ivy's hand for the first time in twenty years. It says only: *Ask him where Mira went.*

title: The Overdue Books
summary: Eolande's library has lost eleven books. She has a list of borrowers, and a lot of patience.

title: Notes in the Margins
summary: The library's cookbook has margin notes in Eolande's hand. They are not about cooking.

title: The Reading Room Audit
summary: An Academy archivist is coming to inventory the Brindlewick library. Eolande has one night to decide what it contains.

title: The Cookbook Question
summary: "Mina" asked Eolande for the cookbook by name. Mina has never cooked in her life.

title: Six Years at D
summary: The morning after the brawl you find Brutus swinging at a post behind the Griffon, alone.

title: The Fifth Attempt
summary: Brutus has booked the C trial again. He asks you to be his second in the Gauntlet's last room.

title: The Buried Sword
summary: After the tenth defeat Hollis digs up the third post. The sword underneath is not his.

title: The Sack We Don't Open
summary: Every granary in Aldmere keeps one sealed sack that is never opened. Millbrook's is the one the goblins keep trying to reach.

title: Brindlewick's Got Talent
summary: Rosie needs a judge for the town's talent show. One of the contestants is not what they seem.

title: Rosie's Second Verse
summary: Rosie dropped a verse tonight. It is the one that means *someone is watching*.

title: Left-Handed Forms
summary: Wendel brings you three forms signed in the wrong hand. He is too polite to say whose.

title: Junior Receptionist Day
summary: Tamsin wants to be Mina when she grows up. Today she is Mina and you are an extremely impressive rookie.

title: Bo's Moon Drawings
summary: Bo only talks to Whiskers. He draws the two moons, over and over. Whiskers watches you until you notice.

title: A Home Soon
summary: Lark tells everyone she will be adopted on the next Blood Vesper. She is so happy that nobody has the heart to ask where.

title: Yesterday's Bread
summary: Hugo takes yesterday's bread to the orphanage every noon. Today his hands are full and a queue has formed.

title: The Wolves' Second Race
summary: Pim has stolen a bounty from under you again, and apologised, and Dax has finally decided to race you for it.

title: A Story for a Scale
summary: Old Sal will trade you a scale from the Rainbow Koi, if you tell him a story he has not heard.

title: The Fog Merchant's Coin
summary: A fox-kin peddler sells things she swears she found. One of them sings when you hold it.

title: The Name of the Blade
summary: Brannoc will not sell a blade to anyone who has not told him its name. He asks yours.

title: Bread on the Step
summary: Nan's bread vanishes from a ruined waystation step every night. The thief is an eighty-year-late courier with a letter for her grandmother.

title: Glowcap Night
summary: Millbrook's children gather glowcaps for the Lantern of the Year. One twin wants the prize; the other wants to free a moth.

title: The White Stag
summary: Wren has tracked the White Stag for ten years without ever drawing her bow. The stag is guarding the last white fawns from poachers.

title: The Mill That Ran Backwards
summary: Millbrook's wheel turns backwards every night. A displaced river child is doing it to be noticed.

title: Lost in the Hush
summary: A child has walked into the Hush, where sound dies. She is visiting her deaf grandfather in secret.

title: The Last Contract of the Silver Ladle
summary: Four seventy-year-old adventurers go back to a sinkhole to bring home their dead leader's lute, and need someone to watch their backs.

title: Lanterns, Not Lamp Oil
summary: The kobold quarry crew is on strike. They want lanterns instead of lamp oil, and a small hat.

title: The Wolf Who Counted Sheep
summary: A bounty is on a lone wolf that sleeps beside the Cobb flock. The girl who feeds her asks you to look first.

title: Stew Diplomacy
summary: The six Hollowpine goblin clans will not share a table. Grandmother Brub needs one ingredient from each clan for a stew nobody has made in a generation.

title: Eight Lamps and an Empty Niche
summary: Eolande wants the old kingdom's waystation lamps relit. Eight are carved. The ninth niche has been defaced.

title: A Sword Under Every Doorstep
summary: Calla has found a sword under her doorstep. Every farm in the valley has one. The barrow dead remember why.

title: The Ring in the Barrow
summary: A groom has vanished the night before his wedding to ask a barrow's dead for his great-grandfather's ring. They said yes, on one condition.

title: The River Toll Quarrel
summary: Two noble houses and the river guild have argued over a toll for forty years. The ledger shows the money has been going somewhere else.

title: The Wheel Thief of Eastgate
summary: Eleven wheels have vanished from a cartwright's yard. The thief is a nine-year-old building a soapbox racer.

title: The Plough Finds a Ledger
summary: A plough turns up a rotted strongbox and a ledger from the Grey Harvest. It names the family that sold grain at famine prices, and the families that paid.

title: The Friend in the Mirror
summary: The children of a Candle Street orphanage have a friend in the mirror. A pamphlet bearing a hand-mirror sigil has been pushed under the door.

title: Stand Down, Soldier
summary: The Greyhollow dead wait nightly at a crossroads for an order nobody has given. A captain's seal in an old cairn can discharge the lesser dead.

title: The Duelist's Last Request
summary: A retired duelist asks you to lose a mock duel in front of his granddaughter. He has been hiding a gift for forty years.

title: The King Wants to Go Fishing
summary: King Alaric IV has asked for one afternoon of fishing. His valet asks you to get him out of the palace.

title: What the Baron Refused
summary: Ashgrave's sealed letters say he refused an order to seize the valley's grain in the Grey Harvest. The dead who march are still hauling it.

title: The Walking Hut Loses Its Way
summary: The Walking Hut has started walking in circles. It is looking for its sibling, which the Choir's silence swallowed.

title: The Eel Moot
summary: Two families claim the same eel trap. The moot asks a stranger to say, quietly, what they saw.

title: Lanterns in Jars
summary: A farmed wisp hums a lullaby nobody remembers. It is the last song of a drowned boatman, and his daughter has been singing it without knowing why.

title: The Clapper in the Peat
summary: A boy believes the Silence is his fault because he rang the abbey bell last. The clapper was taken by a monk who is still guarding it in the peat.

title: The Witch's Price
summary: A child stole a jar of salve from a witch. Granny Hexel needs an outsider to argue for him in the witches' court.

title: High Water on the Stilts
summary: A flood is coming to three stilt-villages. The player decides who and what goes first, and whether to open the sluice.

title: Tea with the Hag of Lowmere
summary: A bog hag with beautiful manners has invited you to tea, and has been practising for two hundred years.

title: The Ferryman's Holiday
summary: The ferryman who carries Greymoor's dead asks you to take the pole for one night. Each passenger has one thing to say.

title: The Choir Passes
summary: The Choir of Silence passes through the village tonight. A widow wants to hold on to her husband's memory for one more night.

title: The Book of Small Things
summary: A witch-elder believes the best defence against the Choir of Silence is writing down the small things people want to keep.

title: A Thimble of Milk
summary: A shrine-keeper has left a thimble of milk for a legendary giant for sixty years. It always vanishes. The giant is real, and shy.

title: The Beetle Rider's Test
summary: A twelve-year-old is taking the beetle rider's test. The Captain wants you riding close, without her knowing.

title: The Seed Recount
summary: The council's vote on whether to ask the big folk for help has one seed too many. The culprit is a mouse, and the town is divided.

title: The Blue in the Tapestry
summary: A moss-weaver needs the last blue thread to finish her grandmother's tapestry. It nests at the edge of Mother Webcrawler's range.

title: A Cat Called Disaster
summary: A stray kitten the size of a landslide has overturned Fiddlewick's pie cart twice. She is just playing.

title: The Aphid Run
summary: A hailstorm is coming and a thousand aphids must be driven under cover, including a very stubborn bull.

title: The Honey That Wasn't
summary: Mossdeep honey is being mixed with syrup between the hive and the Aldmere market. The Thimblefolk are paid for the full jar and cheated of the difference.

title: The Webcrawler's Larder
summary: Seven beetle riders are being held alive in Mother Webcrawler's larder. A mother asks a big-folk stranger to bring her son home.

title: The Old Shade Grows Cold
summary: The warm springs beneath the Old Shade are cooling. A prospector has tunnelled into the tree's mana-line without knowing it is alive.

title: The Big Folk Are Asked
summary: The Thimblefolk council has written an eleven-page request to the big folk. It is really a peace-offer to Mother Webcrawler.

title: The Crooked Bridge
summary: A living bridge has grown crooked, away from the court and down toward the moonwell hamlets. The court wants it cut.

title: The Girl Who Drank the Moon
summary: A seven-year-old drank from a forbidden moonwell. The well is dark and the child now shines. The court wants the glow returned.

title: A Bow Must Be Asked For
summary: A bowyer's apprentice has to make a war-bow in a week. The ash she wants has said no three times.

title: Two Hundred Years of Silence
summary: A three-hundred-year-old noblewoman hasn't spoken to her sister in two hundred years and can't remember why.

title: The Gentle Spores
summary: A hamlet has grown suspiciously cheerful. A spore garden beneath it is tended by a gardener who doesn't know what he's growing.

title: What the Trees Remember
summary: A dryad dreams of something older than the elves. She asks you to follow the dream to its end, and the quest never explains it.

title: The Pilgrim and the World Tree
summary: A human carpenter has walked four hundred miles to reach the World Tree. He won't say why.

title: A Cup of Sunwine
summary: A guest has collapsed at the Queen's garden party over a cup of sunwine meant for the Prince.

title: The Rootward Watch
summary: A spore-touched beast herd is coming for a moonwell hamlet. The Rootward Watch has forty archers and one night.

title: The Last Planting
summary: An elf who has planted a tree every year for nine hundred years has one seed left, and wants to plant it at the edge of the blight.

title: A Coin for Every Deal
summary: A coin-diver finds a singing deal-coin from an eight-hundred-year-old unpaid bargain. The sea-spirit is still waiting.

title: The Counter-Song
summary: A street singer has found a counter-melody that breaks the Drowned Choir's call. The singing ban says she's breaking the law.

title: A Glass Heart for the Lagoon
summary: A merfolk groom has commissioned a glass heart that beats, for a sea-elf bride. The glassblower has never made one.

title: Which Doge?
summary: The Doge has three masked doubles, and one has died. The real Doge is hiding in a cellar.

title: Under the Rooftops
summary: A diver-captain has found a house in the drowned city with a lit window. The family inside is still at dinner.

title: The Deaf Gondolier
summary: A deaf gondolier, immune to the Choir's song, wants to be asked as a gondolier, not a charm.

title: The Auction of Masks
summary: A seamstress can't say her own name. It's on a lot at a secret auction where names are sold.

title: The Three Gaps
summary: Pirates are coming for all three sandbar gaps at once. The raid is a diversion for a honey ship.

title: The Last Song of Isolde Verro
summary: Lirian's greatest soprano has walked into the canal to finish a hymn with the Drowned Choir.

title: Maelsday, All at Once
summary: On Maelsday every lantern in Lirian is lit at once. This year someone is sabotaging the lighting.

title: The Foal Nobody Named
summary: A wild foal has followed a ten-year-old into camp. By custom only the wind may name it, and she won't eat until it does.

title: Champion of Pasture Nine
summary: Two clans claim the same pasture. The rival champion has been paid to win, and the silver is Kade's.

title: The Eagle-Feather Trade
summary: Eleven sacred eagles have died this season and their feathers are on sale. The thief is a fourteen-year-old with a debt.

title: The Ledger Is Longer Than the Whip
summary: A clan mother's granddaughter was sold at the Deep Well. She wants the ledger that names everyone Kade has traded.

title: The Grandmother's Seat
summary: A dying clan elder's seat goes to the winner of an arm-wrestle. A scholar heir faces her warrior cousin, and the old woman has set a second test.

title: Stampede Season
summary: A saiga stampede is thundering toward the Dusksong camp. The fire that spooked it was set on purpose.

title: The Wind Carries the Dead
summary: An old man carries his wife's ashes to a stone marker where she once heard the wind speak. He is afraid of going alone.

title: Kade's Water Tax
summary: Kade has taxed the Deep Well. The clans are tempted to deny his men water, which would break the oath they swore to defend.

title: The Last Free Stallion
summary: A rider has chased the last wild stallion of the Old Herd for three years. Kade's slavers are hunting him tonight.

title: The Moot of Nine Fires
summary: The clans meet in a full moot for the first time in a generation to decide whether to march on the Deep Well.

title: The Stone She Carried
summary: A master smith's first-forge hearth-stone is missing, which is an omen. The finder is an orc child who thought it was pretty.

title: Three Hundred and One Mugs
summary: A gnome has drunk one mug more than the Great Hall's two-hundred-year record. The record mug has a false bottom.

title: The Tap Code
summary: Eleven miners are trapped below the Ashen Mines, tapping a new code. Something deeper is tapping back.

title: Amend the Law
summary: A six-hundred-year-old law forbids gnomes from lighting flame in the main halls. A plaque might interpret it without amending it.

title: The Giant's Envoy
summary: Skarn has sent an envoy under a white banner, offering to withdraw his army if the Thane lends him the furnace-heart for one night.

title: The Seal Is Warm
summary: The seal on the deepest shaft is warm and getting warmer. A single hammer-stroke answers from behind it.

title: Runes in Cold Iron
summary: An apprentice has rebuilt half of a forbidden rune-technique from scrap. The masters want it kept buried.

title: A Flame From Every Forge
summary: The furnace-heart is guttering. Dorn needs a flame from each of nineteen clan forges, carried by a non-dwarf, to relight it.

title: The Thane's Granddaughter
summary: Skarn's orcs have taken the Thane's granddaughter hostage. The Thane cannot spend an army on a rescue.

title: The Anvil That Counted
summary: The Great Anvil has counted every blow for a thousand years except the first. Old Baldur asks the player to strike it.

title: The Last Pillar
summary: The great shrine's last pillar was left bare, and the priests call it unlucky. The carpenter has forgotten why he did it.

title: The Spirit Who Had No Seat
summary: A nine-year-old organiser has counted seventy-one seats and seventy-two spirits. The extra is a shy umbrella-spirit.

title: The Kappa's Bow
summary: A kappa has blocked the ford three times. A boatman's bow is too shallow, and a deep bow would spill the water in the kappa's dish.

title: The Mask-Carver
summary: A carver has been ordered to make three hundred identical masks for Kurogane. The masks work best when carved without love.

title: Fourteen People and a Festival
summary: A village of fourteen must host the spirit festival tomorrow, or the spirits will forget it.

title: The Tengu's Test
summary: A tengu swordmaster teaches a technique that does not strike. He asks the player to lose first.

title: The Sword Given to the Gods
summary: A swordsmith will not sell his masterwork to the oni. He asks the player to give it to the gods instead.

title: The Masked Village
summary: A village has been masked by Kurogane. A priestess searches its streets for the one child who is still laughing.

title: The Hundredth Lantern
summary: Once a century a hundred lanterns walk to the shogun's castle. The hundredth must be carried by someone who belongs nowhere.

title: A Letter Written in Courtesy
summary: An oni warlord has sent a perfectly polite letter. It asks for a reply, and for understanding.

title: Wood for the Last Fire
summary: The Last Fire has two logs left. The sacred grove that supplies it is in Ymgrir's territory.

title: The Frozen Fleet
summary: Forty fishing boats and two hundred sailors are frozen in the outer fjord. A channel must be cut before the next storm.

title: A Frost Troll at the Door
summary: A frost troll has knocked on a goodwife's door. By the law of the hearth, no guest may be turned away.

title: A Burning Ship on Ice
summary: A jarl's funeral ship must reach open water to burn. The fjord is frozen for two leagues.

title: A Saga About the Living
summary: A skald wants to write a saga about someone who is still alive, and asks the player to help choose whom.

title: The Survivor Who Came Back Older
summary: A man from the fleet that sailed north forty years ago has come back, aged forty years in what he says was three weeks.

title: A Cave of Summer
summary: A glacier guide has found a warm cave with green grass inside the ice. It is the skalds' hundred-year summer, and it is dying.

title: The Thing
summary: The jarls have called the Thing to elect a war-king. A neutral witness is needed for a vote that could go three ways, or none.

title: The Last Fire Goes Out
summary: Ymgrir's blizzard has reached Skjaldheim. The Last Fire must not go out.

title: The Saga, Sung
summary: The skald will sing her saga of the living at the closing feast. She has one verse left, and wants the player to write it.

title: The Table Set for Six
summary: A caravan guide's echo sits at a laid table with an empty chair. The sixth guide went for water and never came back.

title: The Lighthouse That Wasn't Lit
summary: A lighthouse has been dark for thirty years. The keeper's log says she stopped lighting it on purpose.

title: Ninety-Nine Steps
summary: A quiet stair in Shen-Lu has ninety-nine carved stories and a blank hundredth step. The voice that counts them has never reached the end.

title: The Wedding Tent
summary: A wedding tent stands on a ridge in the Strife Marches, set for two rival companies. The couple never arrived.

title: A Quiet Place to Wait
summary: An old sled-dog sits beside an overturned sled on the ice, waiting for a whaler who said he would be back by supper.

title: Heads, Tails and the Edge
summary: Vex has set a wager over a fisherman's debt. The coin lands on its edge, and the god has a plan.

title: A Lantern for the Unclaimed
summary: A lantern-sister has lit a lantern for every body she found on the Marches' battlefields. One hundred have no name.

title: The Smallest Job
summary: Thorgrim asks for one perfect repair of a child's broken toy-clock, with no magic and no shortcuts.

title: A Banner for the Coward
summary: A soldier who fled a battle carrying a wounded friend asks to walk the storm under Kaelthas's banner to be cleared of cowardice.

title: The Dream That Was Yours
summary: Maelis sends the player a dream of a stranger about to fail the great examination. The god asks only for a kindness.

title: Six Lanterns of the Examination Hall
summary: The Examination Hall's doors will not open when its six virtue-lanterns are lit in the usual order. A poem on the lintel says to begin where the learned stop.

title: The River That Remembered Its Bed
summary: A dry, unmapped aqueduct keeps trying to flood toward a garden that is not on any plan. Three sluices, three elements.

title: The Thread That Hums
summary: One thread in Umbravel's web hums a single wrong note. Five more threads, plucked in order, open a pouch with a mother's unfinished lullaby.

title: The Ball Court of the River-Kings
summary: A priest has found the hidden court of the river-kings' oldest ceremony, a ball-game with three rules, one forgotten.

title: Cairn of Winds
summary: A bolted cairn at the top of Stormreach has never been opened. A storm is coming, and a bolt can be steered.

title: The Longest Lunch
summary: Lyra decides to eat at every one of Hall Square's thirty-one stalls in a day. It is a joke she is making to herself about money.

title: First Snow
summary: The first snow of the year falls on Moraveil. Kiri has never seen snow from somewhere warm, with nothing to fear.

title: The Honest Game
summary: Bram wants to lose a card game fairly, to prove his luck isn't a trick. His luck refuses.

title: A Pint With the Captain
summary: Aldric wants to walk past his old guard-post once, with someone beside him, and say nothing.

title: A Nail for the Anvil
summary: Torvald offers to teach the player to forge a single nail. It takes all night, and a wrapped blade stays in the corner.

title: The Beast That Ate the Bridge
summary: A beast has been wrecking a farm-bridge every night. The stones are moved, not broken, and a very large egg lies by a flooded cave.

title: The Tithe-Hound
summary: A stone hound follows the duchy's reeve through the streets. It is the land's creditor, and four generations of tithes are unpaid.

title: The Head That Grew Back
summary: One head of the mire's hydra smashes canoes. It is always the left, and it always grows back, because nobody has fed it in four hundred years.

title: Back Pay for the Dead
summary: A phantom ship sends invoices to the harbour clerk. Its crew is owed forty-one years of unpaid wages.

title: A Calf Lost on the Ice
summary: A floe has followed an ice-fishing village for three weeks, against the current. It is a lost leviathan calf.

title: The Nobody Test
summary: The Shadow Syndicate's test: take a lender's ledger, and leave a gift in its place.

title: The Thesis Defence
summary: The Academy admits outsiders by argument. The player must defend something they honestly believe before the Hall of Questions.

title: The Honest Scale
summary: The Consortium wants a market audited quietly. One scale of forty is off by two grains, and the owner doesn't know.

title: The Candle Count
summary: The Church sends the player to audit a poor parish whose books have never balanced, because its priest feeds fifty people a week.

title: The Alpha's Dinner
summary: The Beastkin Federation's Alpha invites the player to dinner. There are forty small courtesies, and he will notice every one.

title: The Puppet on the Milestone
summary: A marionette sits on a milestone each dawn, waiting. Its puppeteer's master died before finishing the last scene.

title: The Cart That Pulled Itself
summary: A ghost carter on the White Duchies' road is sixty years late delivering a wedding cake.

title: The Collector of Last Words
summary: An old woman at a roadside table collects people's last words. She asks the player for theirs.

title: The Mimic Who Wanted a Friend
summary: A mimic that looks like a chest has waited two hundred years to be opened kindly.

title: The Highwayman Who Took Only Burdens
summary: A highwayman on the Marches road takes only the heaviest thing a traveller carries, and keeps it safe.

title: A Basket for the Bridge-Keeper
summary: Marta sends a basket to the Millbrook bridge-keeper, a troll whose toll is one true story.

title: Seed Swap
summary: Seed Swap Day in Brindlewick. Five households want what the others have, and nobody will say so.

title: A Hum for the Koi
summary: Old Sal thinks a shy Rainbow Koi will come to a hummed song. He can't hum; the player can.

title: A Cake for Tamsin
summary: Tamsin turns ten and has never had a cake. Hugo needs honey, vanilla and eggs, and it must be a surprise.

title: Roof Day
summary: The mill roof has seven leaks and the rain is coming. Jory needs the whole town, and someone who can ask.

title: The Word for "Truce"
summary: An eleven-year-old translator finds that the human and goblin words for "truce" mean different things.

title: Mushrooms and Malice
summary: A human merchant is accused of poisoning the goblins' mushrooms. Someone else wants the truce to fail.

title: The Worm's Lesson
summary: The goblins' oldest story says a great worm taught them something nobody remembers. The mural at the end of her tunnel says what.

title: Ladders and Stairs
summary: The humans want a stair up to the goblin village; the goblins have ladders. A counterweight lift needs both sides to pull.

title: Sixteen Years of Quiet
summary: The two founders of the truce haven't spoken for sixteen years. One of them wants to know why the other never said sorry.

title: The Warband at the Gate
summary: A hill-goblin warband has marched to Moraveil to join Grakkus. Their captain asks for a parley she half-regrets.

title: Drill Day
summary: The council wants a joint goblin-human militia trained in a week, in two languages, before Grakkus arrives.

title: A Safe Road for a Sick Child
summary: An orc mother brings a feverish child to Moraveil's goblin healers, and must cross a bridge with a crowd.

title: Two Children, One Rope
summary: The two founders want the rope that pulled a child from the Flooded Cave forty years ago, to hang on the Truce Bridge.

title: What the Disaster Left
summary: Three hundred survivors of two smashed goblin villages are walking toward Moraveil with nothing, and an escort is needed.

title: The Coin From Every Kingdom
summary: Someone is digging the grave-coins up on the Field of Coins and leaving buttons behind as an apology.

title: Two Barons, One Village
summary: Two barons claim one village. The headwoman wants to ask the village instead, and needs a witness to keep the peace.

title: The Man Whose Father Sings
summary: A farmer's dead father sings at night, under the Choir's chain-rhythm, a lullaby he never finished.

title: A Contract With an Exit
summary: A mercenary captain wants out of her contract before the Choir reaches her fort. The contract has no exit clause.

title: The Horse That Broke the Peace
summary: The great peace of Castle Varn broke over a horse. The ghost steward wants the innocent mare's name cleared.

title: Smuggler's Honour
summary: A smuggler must carry a crate of medicine across three borders in one day, past three very different customs men.

title: The Deserter's Song
summary: A deserter has written an off-beat march that trips the Choir's chant. He needs a crowd to sing it, and can't show his face.

title: Wheat on the Field of Coins
summary: A retired mercenary wants to grow wheat on a quarter-acre of the Field of Coins. The sexton thinks he is a ghoul.

title: A Chapel in the Cellar
summary: A village keeps its chapel in a cellar. The Choir's song makes people forget to pray, and a hundred voices must sing one hymn.

title: The Choir's Quiet Door
summary: A young woman has followed the East Road for six weeks looking for her brother, who joined the Choir of Chains for belonging.

title: The Kaelsday Round
summary: A tithe-clerk insists on collecting every box in a cracking ward and finds that people have been leaving stones instead of coin.

title: Down in the Gallery
summary: A quarry-worker's family is alive under a collapsed cellar, held up by a golem that will not let go of the roof.

title: The Ledger in the Walls
summary: The cracks in Ashgrove run block to block by quarry, and their lengths add up to the town's unpaid tithe.

title: A Long Night at Oakes Farm
summary: Frightened stone-gnawers crowd toward a wheat farm, and a farmer's whole plan is a goose.

title: Condemned, With Regret
summary: A lending-house must call the loan on a leaning house, and the notary asks a stranger to help her decide what the law is for.

title: The Eleventh Clause
summary: The original tithe contract has an eleventh clause, struck from every copy, that says how the tithe was supposed to be paid.

title: The Quiet Petition
summary: The Grand Duke wants the Colossus stopped without admitting any debt, and the wording of a petition decides who gets paid.

title: The Last Mason of the Old Rite
summary: An old mason can no longer climb to the Foundation Stone, and asks the player to help lay the abolished offering.

title: Hollin Cross Pays Its Tithe
summary: A drowned quarry town is eerily tidy, and its last ledger says the tithe was paid in full the night it fell.

title: The Order of Evacuation
summary: A ducal list puts the quarry-workers last out of a doomed town, on a road that will break first.

title: Dawn-Lamp Hour
summary: A lamplighter's moths desert his lanterns for one enormous, brooding cave-moth.

title: A Family in the Cocoon
summary: A silk-dyer's wife and daughter are alive inside a cocoon, and the guilds say cutting it would insult the Queen.

title: Honey for the Deep Webs
summary: A stranded surface trader has forty jars of honey the Queen's brood keep asking about, and the guilds want it as leverage.

title: Who Cut the Bridge?
summary: A bridge to Weavers' Row was cut with a blade, not a claw, and the guilds blame the Queen.

title: A Line of Daylight
summary: The city's blind bats are leaving upward, toward a crack in the cavern roof where a bar of sunlight falls at noon.

title: Restored, Quietly
summary: A guildmistress wants the broken silk contract restored without public vote, and the families who lost homes would never be told.

title: The Vigil at Lift Nine
summary: The brood climbs the cables of the lift that carries lower-web families to safety, and the lift-warden will not close it.

title: The Knot She Always Tied
summary: An old blind weaver has left a silk offering at the edge of the deep webs every night for fifty years, and tonight someone answers.

title: Chain or Silk
summary: A gnome engineer wants to replace a lift's silk cables with chain, and the spider that runs it has not been told.

title: A Letter in the Web
summary: The deep webs have sent a knotted strand to the Contract Hall, and reading it shows the Queen's opening terms.

title: A Hot Meal and No Crew
summary: A crewless ship with a hot dinner on its table raises a salvage-law claim, and the captain's reason for leaving it was a hunch.

title: Neutral Ground
summary: A pirate captain and a port councillor both want a truce and neither will walk first onto the other's end of a rope bridge.

title: Three Bidders Dead
summary: A flagship map has killed three bidders, and its missing margin carried a warning the auctioneer cut away.

title: Whose Boots Are These
summary: A child finds eighty-year-old boots on the tide-line and the custom says someone must walk them home.

title: The Parrot Who Kept the Books
summary: A parrot has been reciting the council's true accounts, which show the port's income is half what has been announced.

title: The Bridges of Saltreach
summary: Raiders cut the rope-ways of a stilt-town while its children are moved to the port.

title: The Flagship's Bell
summary: A diver-master swears the flagship's bell has rung every night since the Sunken Fleet went down, and the wreck hides a dry cabin and a legible log.

title: The Channel Moves
summary: The brood has crooked the safe channel, and nine grain-ships need a guide through shifting water.

title: A Tribute Proposed
summary: A salvage captain proposes paying the Krakenmother one cargo in ten, and the council's vote is tied.

title: The Sea's Coins
summary: Someone has been taking the coins divers drop for the sea, and the thieves are hungry children watched by something very large.

title: The Year Nobody Recited
summary: The oasis's shoreline recital has a softened year in it, and a young apprentice cannot bring himself to say the true number.

title: The Unpaid Tithe
summary: The last survivor of a lost caravan is walking its water-tithe to Qadira on foot, and the oasis is too short of water to want it.

title: A Dowry in Salt
summary: Two nomad tribes will not agree on a bride-price because it includes one sour old camel that neither will give away.

title: The Night the Awning Held
summary: A glass-laden sandstorm bears down on a caravanserai with two hundred guests and one old awning.

title: What the Glass Remembers
summary: A hermit's nine years of notes from the humming Glass Streaks turn out to be directions to a buried water-road.

title: The Last Sunrise on the Streaks
summary: A blind old caravan guide wants to hear the sun come up over the Glass Streaks one last time.

title: A Shovel Under Seal
summary: A treasure-hunter and the water-keepers disagree over whether a buried machine should be opened, and neither knows what it is.

title: The Walker's Road
summary: A keeper charts the Colossus's footprints and learns that it walks a fixed route to a city that no longer exists.

title: The Eighth Well
summary: A nomad elder asks the player to find the eighth well her people sing of and decide whether a thousand-year promise still holds.

title: The Ration Council
summary: With two wells dry, a young keeper-elect must divide the oasis's last water among gardeners, caravans, the sick and the tribes, and asks a witness to sit with her.

title: The Bird Who Knew the Manual
summary: Three sects blame each other for a missing manual, which has been hiding in a teahouse mynah's memory.

title: A Herb That Does Not Grow
summary: A master climbs a grey peak to fetch a spirit herb for his ill student, and finds there is none and never was.

title: The First Bout in Forty Years
summary: Three sects hold a tiny friendly bout for the first time in forty years, and each has sent a saboteur to spoil it.

title: The Hand Behind the Hunger
summary: An elder asks the player to learn which rival sect made the Colossus, and the trails all lead back to the single school they once shared.

title: Letters Between Two Graves
summary: A gardener finds sealed letters beneath each of the two founders' graves, each addressed to the other, and asks the player to carry them across.

title: A Bucket for Every Step
summary: The water-carriers of a sect stair put down their buckets and ask only to be thanked by name.

title: The Tiger on the Grey Pass
summary: A starving spirit tiger drifts toward villages for warmth, and a huntress will not hunt it.

title: The Night the Mountain Walked
summary: A village climbs the stair in the dark to escape the Hunger Colossus's path, using rope, drums and oil-lamps instead of qi-lanterns.

title: Hands Without Qi
summary: A small sect that teaches the body before qi asks the greater sects to try its way, now that Wuxiang eats qi.

title: Tea for Three Precedences
summary: A tea-seller must serve three sects the first cup at the same noon and needs a way to do it without insulting any.

title: The Candidate's Road
summary: A candidate and his formidable mother must reach the Examination Hall along a ridge road watched by demons.

title: The Exile's Survey
summary: A scholar exiled for proving the wall faced the wrong enemy wants to come home and survey it for the real one.

title: Shoes at the Cloud Gate
summary: An outland mercenary will not take off his boots at a guesthouse where nobody has ever worn them past the sill.

title: A Guest in the Rice Loft
summary: A shy mountain spirit hiding from demons has tidied a farmer's rice loft into towers, and the farmer wants it gone.

title: The Paper Varos Set
summary: Varos has sent the capital an eleven-question examination paper, and the chief examiner needs help answering it.

title: Terrace Seven Holds
summary: Forty soldiers hold a granary terrace for one night so six hundred sacks of barley can be moved down the pass.

title: Tablets Down the Pass
summary: A widow asks the player to slip into a demon-held gate-town and carry her family's seven ancestor tablets down the pass.

title: Drums on the Wall
summary: On the anniversary of the winter the wall held, the garrison plays the drum-vigil while a raid tries to silence it.

title: The Watchman Who Still Faces North
summary: An old watchman has faced north for sixty years, long after the wrong enemy was known, and a young sentry wants to know why.

title: Shrines at Every Bend
summary: A shrine-keeper asks the player to hold the last twelve of the pass's forty bend-shrines through one dark night.

title: The Rose That Bled
summary: A bed of roses on the palace terrace bleeds when cut, because it has been drinking water that belongs to somebody else.

title: Two Houses, One Tribute
summary: Two perfume-houses each insist on filling the whole rosewater tribute for Zahhar. Each has been quietly wondering how the other's smells.

title: The Nightingale Who Would Not Sing
summary: The palace nightingales have gone silent since the fountains were hushed. They are waiting for the water to start.

title: A Cup for the Poet's Garden
summary: A dying poet's last student wants one cup of water for every rose in her teacher's grave-garden. The ration allows water for food only.

title: Seven Wells, One Song
summary: A locked channel in a mountain village opens only when seven wells are sounded in the order of a children's rhyme, and the village has no reason to share it.

title: The Unarmed Caravan
summary: The tribute caravan must go unarmed by treaty custom, and a band of water-sellers plans to rob it at the Narrow Stair.

title: The Poem Zahhar Asked For
summary: A famous poet has answered Zahhar's summons with a poem. Her students want her home before she writes it.

title: Forty Days Again
summary: A cracked section of the Great Aqueduct must be mended in three nights while Zahhar's stone-bearers watch from the ledge.

title: The Basin from the Caves
summary: A silver basin taken from a div-cave is the other half of the garden treaties. A scholar wants it back at the gate and a board wants it kept.

title: Who Drinks First
summary: The water-masters' sum says one city must go dry. The Forty Days' old rota says otherwise, if every city keeps it.

title: The Part From Below
summary: An upper-city inventor needs a coil from the Undercity and is afraid to fetch it. The coil-winder has never been named on anything.

title: Thank You, Number Nine
summary: The council is stripping forty lifts and pumps for barricades. Undercity custom says each must be thanked first.

title: Seven Faces, One Slow
summary: The seventh face of the great clock loses four minutes a day. The founders' instructions survive in a nursery rhyme.

title: Two Patents, One Gadget
summary: Two inventors claim the same self-winding teapot. Both built it from the same missing page.

title: The Child and the Gremlin
summary: A child has hidden a gremlin that refuses to join the King's song. Everyone else wants to catch it.

title: A Name Worth Keeping
summary: A Clockborn repairer asks its guild-master for its name in writing, not its freedom.

title: What the Council Knew
summary: The boiler-tenders' union wants proof that the council knew about the gremlins and did nothing. The proof is in the lever register.

title: The Names Under the Soot
summary: A generation ago an engine exploded and the council listed thirty-one names. The soot-wall holds two hundred and twelve.

title: Medicine for the Rattle
summary: A surgeon needs cold water and medicine carried through gremlin pipe-ways to the Cog-Touched quarter, past a council cleaner.

title: The Last Car Down
summary: The council orders the funicular stopped at the third tier. A conductor with six hundred people on the platform refuses.

title: The Garden That Drifted
summary: A floating garden has drifted into another city's canal, and the three-dawns rule is about to hand it over.

title: The Match on the Far Side
summary: A ball team must cross the hydra's hunting-water to play the spring match against a rival city.

title: A Blanket by Canoe
summary: A grandmother's blanket must cross cut water to reach a great-grandchild, with a whole city's letters in the same canoe.

title: The Posts Have Moved
summary: Someone is moving the canoe-road posts at night. The new line is a little safer.

title: Clay Beans
summary: A market is flooded with baked-clay cacao beans, made by a potter who just wanted to feed his children.

title: The Priest Who Came Back
summary: An exiled priest wants to restore the feeding rites. The city does not know what they really were.

title: What the Star-Counters Saw
summary: Two observatories' tables, lined up by half a day, show the hydra hunts hardest on dark-moon nights.

title: Flowers for the Night Causeway
summary: The night flower market runs beside the hydra's lagoon. Four hundred sellers must load the morning offering without a sound.

title: The Ring of Equal Water
summary: The league of river-cities meets for the first time in a generation, and no king wants the most honoured seat.

title: The Boy Who Stopped Feeding the River
summary: A grieving boy has stopped putting flowers on the water. His father is alive on a mud island at the end of the channel.

title: The Storm-Caller Who Went Quiet
summary: A storm-caller has lost her power and blames the roc. She hasn't mourned her brother.

title: A Rope Along the Cliffs
summary: A fishing fleet is trapped in a cove. A three-mile rope must be carried along the cliffs, anchored by a chain of volunteers.

title: The Egg in the Gatherer's Basket
summary: An egg-gatherer found a roc's egg, abandoned and cold. The council argues over destroying it.

title: The Best Rope in the World
summary: A rope-master who has won eleven years running secretly wants someone to beat him.

title: Struck, and Blessed
summary: A man struck by lightning is treated as a saint by the whole town. He would like to go fishing.

title: The Guano Accords
summary: Two cliff-towns have quarrelled for eleven years over a single cliff of nesting birds.

title: Rod Forest
summary: Forty apprentice storm-callers are in the Rod Forest when a storm worse than forecast arrives, and one of them won't come in.

title: A Funeral for the Lightning
summary: A dead storm-caller must be carried to a peak for the lightning, in the worst storm of the year.

title: The Fledgling's Feather
summary: A young thunderbird with a broken wing is stuck on a ledge. A feather freely given is the only shield against the roc's lightning.

title: The Nest Seen by Lightning
summary: The Roc's Nest is visible only by lightning flashes. A councillor of seventy wants a drawing by morning.

title: A Divorce From the Sea
summary: A fisher who lost a husband and a son to the water wants to divorce the sea. The vow has no exit.

title: The Berg With Something Inside
summary: A Bone Berg drifting toward a village hums a single note. A frozen sky-whale is waking inside it.

title: Quiet Feet
summary: The leviathan is drawn to footsteps. A grandmother who can cross the ice without waking it has one week to teach three villages.

title: The Sixteenth Year
summary: A sixteen-year-old must marry the sea this week. Her father drowned two winters ago, and she doesn't want to lie.

title: A Doll for the Sea
summary: A six-year-old thinks the sea is lonely and offers it her best doll. The sea writes back.

title: The Broken Floe
summary: A scholar has mapped the leviathan's surfacings and thinks it hunts in a spiral, following warmth.

title: Ice Wyrm Season
summary: Hungry ice wyrms are hunting a winter camp of three hundred. The warden wants them turned, not killed.

title: A Wedding Under the Aurora
summary: Two fishers married to the sea are to wed under the aurora. The sea, by custom, must give them away.

title: The Boat-Eaters' Reckoning
summary: Sixty years ago a frozen fleet's crews survived by eating their boats. A hidden log says there was something else.

title: What the Bone Bergs Carry
summary: A cartographer has assembled on a beach the skeleton of something that does not exist. She needs one last bone.

title: Sea Legs, Sand Legs
summary: A purser needs help guiding seasick land-dwellers through the swaying town without losing their dignity.

title: The Calendar of Her Songs
summary: An archivist compares nine generations of Thalassa's songs and finds her silences fall before Glassmaw comes.

title: A Lullaby the Whale Does Not Know
summary: An apprentice not yet allowed to sing to Thalassa has written her a song and needs a lookout.

title: Barnacle Rot
summary: Barnacle anchors are failing; starving sand-rays are eating the roots.

title: The Glass Garden
summary: Glassmaw's trails have fused into a beautiful garden of glass that the next storm will shatter.

title: Sand-Fish Season
summary: Glittering sand-fish run for three days and the netmaster is short of hands.

title: A Death Sung Wrong
summary: A whale-singer sang a death into Thalassa's ear in the wrong key and cannot forgive herself.

title: The Captain's Vote
summary: A contested captaincy turns on whether to steer the sand-whale toward the sea.

title: The Other Town
summary: The oldest rider wants to see where the second whale-town fell.

title: What She Hums at Night
summary: The night-singer hears Thalassa hum a four-phrase song no one taught her.

title: Boots at the Door
summary: A doorkeeper needs help hushing a pilgrim festival so that nothing echoes off the bones.

title: Chips From a Rib
summary: Relics are vanishing from ribs no miner could reach; the thief has a reason.

title: The Lullaby Cantor's Cold
summary: The cantor's voice fails on the lowest note of the evening lullaby.

title: Fire-Lily Harvest
summary: Fire-lilies bloom for one night on the vents and the herbalist needs careful hands.

title: A Pilgrim Who Cannot Climb
summary: A pilgrim with a ruined knee wants to walk the whole Bone Road.

title: The Abbots Split
summary: The council is split between fighting Vyrmax and bargaining with him; the abbot asks for honest witnesses.

title: The Drake Who Came to the Gate
summary: A starving drake hatchling has come to the monastery gate alone.

title: The Book of the Burned Monk
summary: A monk burned by a fire from the rock left a ritual book; a second reader compares it to the lullaby.

title: The Warm Vertebra
summary: A brass probe says one vertebra is warmer than any in ninety years of records.

title: What the Mountain Dreams
summary: The eldest monk asks the player to sit in the skull's eye socket until the mountain talks in its sleep.

title: The Recruit Who Could Not Swear
summary: A recruit who passed every drill will not speak the barracks pledge.

title: Horn Practice
summary: A horn-warden teaches the town's children the alarm calls without frightening them.

title: A Grain Wagon for Fort Seven
summary: Fort Seven is two days short of grain and needs one wagon through the pass.

title: The Spy Who Paid His Bill
summary: A too-punctual guest at a diplomats' inn is certainly a spy, but whose?

title: Letters From the Fallen Fort
summary: The last letters of soldiers from two fallen forts must be carried to their families by hand.

title: The Senate Dinner
summary: A senator hosts a dinner at which the empire's next heir is quietly sounded out.

title: Rank and File
summary: A sergeant is offered the commission of the man who died in his place.

title: The General Who Wanted to Retire
summary: A general named as a possible heir would rather keep bees and needs a way out that shames no one.

title: What the Pledge Cost
summary: A chaplain asks for a rubbing of the carved pledge and learns there is a chiselled-out line beneath it.

title: The Night the Horns Failed
summary: After two false alarms, a real one is not believed, and the pass fort needs a gate held.

title: A Mask for a Stranger
summary: A frightened newcomer asks for the smallest mask in the market.

title: The Last Open Chimney
summary: Sweeps have kept a condemned chimney open by hand; tonight the wardens come to close it.

title: Debt of the Old Miners
summary: A miner's family tally of the old miners' greed has a second column nobody has read.

title: Smuggler's Lullaby
summary: A smuggler of refugees carries a child who will not stop singing through the wardens' tunnels.

title: The Ash-Moth Census
summary: A naturalist counts ash moths and finds they avoid the districts with closed chimneys.

title: A Mask Without a Face
summary: A thief who gives away stolen masks has been found out by a warden.

title: Alchemist's Apprentice
summary: An alchemist's accident-prone apprentice is secretly trying to build a filter for the choked districts.

title: Choking District
summary: A doctor in a closed district needs hand-pumped bellows to ventilate his ward.

title: The Fire That Will Not Pay
summary: The oldest miner says the fire is an invitation no one answered and walks to the first seam.

title: What Vasque Keeps in the Smoke
summary: A voice in a flue keeps three lost things for someone it cannot remember.
